title: Blackeye Pea, Canned, Sodium Added, Drained and Rinsed

content.title: About
content.content: Blackeye pea is a variety of dry pea that is often canned with added salt. After canning the peas are typically drained and rinsed to reduce sodium content. The peas have a dark green color, a mildly sweet flavor and a firm texture, making them suitable as a side dish or an ingredient in salads and soups.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Blackeye peas belong to the legume family and are closely related to regular green peas.
Canned peas are a staple in military rations because of their long shelf life.
Draining and rinsing canned peas can cut the sodium level by up to 30 % compared with the original brine.
Peas are rich in plant protein and fiber, which makes them popular in vegetarian diets.
In the United States black‑eyed peas are considered a symbol of good luck for New Year's celebrations.

items.title: Rich in plant protein
items.content: One cup of canned blackeye peas provides about 13 g of protein, supporting muscle maintenance.

items.title: High in dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber promotes healthy digestion and helps keep you feeling full.

items.title: Source of folate (vitamin B9)
items.content: Folate is essential for DNA synthesis and is especially important for pregnant women.

items.title: Contains iron
items.content: Iron from plant sources supports oxygen transport in the blood.

items.title: Low glycemic index
items.content: Peas raise blood sugar slowly, which is beneficial for people managing diabetes.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Even after rinsing, some salt remains; individuals on a low‑sodium diet should account for it in their total intake.

items.title: Legume allergy
items.content: Some people may experience allergic reactions to peas, ranging from skin rash to swelling.

items.title: Phytic acid
items.content: Peas contain phytic acid, which can reduce the absorption of certain minerals when consumed in large amounts.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: After draining and rinsing, the peas are less salty. They can be tossed into salads, added to soups and stews, served as a side dish, or mashed into a spread. They pair well with vegetables, meats, rice, and a variety of herbs and spices.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store unopened cans in a cool, dry place. Once opened, transfer the peas to an airtight container and keep them in the refrigerator for up to 4‑5 days. Discard if you notice off‑odors or mold.
